subject: Urgent: Olive Health production latency spike — rapid lifeline coordination
messages:
From: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@olivehealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Claire Mendez <claire.mendez@olivehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency and 500s affecting checkout (URGENT)

Lauren —

We started seeing a large spike in 95th/99th latency around 07:45 PDT this morning and a concurrent increase in 500 errors for our checkout flow. Error rate peaked at ~24% for a 20-minute window and we've had multiple customer complaints. Our paged alerts went out.

Attached are a few request ids and a short synthetic trace from our side. Can Redwood confirm whether there were any rolling deploys, config changes, or regional capacity events in us-west-2 around that time? This is impacting a live promo and we need an ETA on remediation and an explanation for the execs.

Examples: req_id: 6f2b9a1c, 6f2b9b2d, 6f2b9c8f

Please escalate — Simon
Simon Lewis
Senior SRE, Olive Health
attachments: diagnostic-snapshot-20270618.json (JSON), sample-trace.txt (txt)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Production latency and 500s affecting checkout (URGENT)

Simon — thanks for the heads up and the trace. I'm pulling the team into a rapid coordination call now.

Immediate answers: no scheduled deploys were pushed from our side in us-west-2 between 07:30–08:00 PDT. We're treating this as a production degradation that needs executive attention.

Planned next steps (happening now):
- Marissa (CS lead) will stand up a customer bridge and gather any additional logs you can paste into the bridge.
- Markus (runtime lead) is doing a hot-path analysis for batching/kv cache behavior and will check for kernel fallback/oom indicators.
- I'll loop Aditya for commercial exec visibility and to prepare an interim credits proposal if needed.

Can you join a 15-min bridge at 08:35 PDT? If not, we'll start at 08:30 and keep you updated in-thread.

Lauren Bishop

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@olivehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 500s affecting checkout (URGENT)

Quick tech readout from the bridge:
- Observed a sudden shift in batch size distribution at ~07:42 where median batch size dropped and tail (99.9th) spiked — suggests some clients started sending many small sequences which increases per-token overhead.
- GPU utilization stayed within expected range; no OOMs. However, we did see a transient kernel fallback on one node (kernel-id: kf_11) that increases token latency by ~30–40ms.
- KV cache hit rate dropped for the affected prefixes — likely correlated with the small-batch/TTL pattern.

Mitigation we pushed at 08:55 PDT:
1) Forced routing of the affected tenant traffic to a warm pool with pre-warmed caches (rolling) — reduced error rate from 24% -> 6% in Canary.
2) Tuned batching window for the tenant to favor slightly larger aggregates (tradeoff: ~10ms median added, but 95/99 improves).
3) Kicked a diagnostic snapshot (attached) and increased debug sampling for 2h.

Next: we'll monitor for 2 hours, progressively roll the routing if stable. If the error rate remains >5% we'll prepare a rollback/instance-replacement plan.

Markus Klein
Senior Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime
attachments: diagnostic-snapshot-20270618.json

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@olivehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, Claire Mendez <claire.mendez@olivehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Production latency and 500s affecting checkout (URGENT) — interim customer update

Simon / Claire —

Thanks for joining the bridge. Short summary for your leadership and customers:
- Impact window: ~07:42–08:00 PDT. Peak error rate ~24% impacting checkout flows.
- Root cause (current hypothesis): client-side pattern shifted to smaller sequences which increased per-request overhead and caused a transient kernel fallback on one node, plus a KV-cache miss storm.
- Immediate mitigation: we routed your traffic to a warm, pre-warmed pool and tightened batching for the tenant. Canary tests show error rate falling to ~6% and 95/99 latencies improving.
- Next 2 hours: elevated sampling and monitoring; we will roll the routing to 50% if the canary remains stable and communicate again at 13:00 PDT.

We are preparing a formal incident readout and will propose an SLA credit to cover the customer impact. Aditya will follow up on the commercial note; attached is a preliminary credit proposal for internal review.

Action for Olive: if you can share any recent client SDK changes or traffic shifts (time of new promo, increased mobile users), that will help confirm hypothesis.

We own the rest. I will provide the 13:00 PDT status update regardless of outcome.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (555) 412-0092
attachments: proposed-sla-credit-OLIVE-DH8231.pdf

From: Claire Mendez <claire.mendez@olivehealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@olivehealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 500s affecting checkout (URGENT) — thanks and next steps

Lauren / team — thank you for the rapid response and the interim mitigation. The canary data looks encouraging and we've not seen additional customer complaints after 08:30. We confirmed a mobile SDK change late yesterday that increased tail fragmentation — we're rolling a client patch to batch locally which should help.

Next steps on our side:
- Patch mobile SDK rollout scheduled for tonight at 23:00 PDT (gradual).
- We'll share post-rollout telemetry at 02:00 PDT and coordinate a follow-up readout.

Claire Mendez
VP Product Operations, Olive Health

Appreciate the clear comms. Please keep us posted on the final incident readout and any follow-through items you recommend (longer term tuning, config defaults, and regression tests).
